extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, agency counsel, contractors, and project sponsors/applicants involved in preparing or adopting EISs, EAs, CEs, FONSIs, and RODs
extracted.subtask_short: NEPA environmental document preparation and adoption
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Federal agencies (and related applicants/contractors) on preparing, supervising, adopting, supplementing, evaluating, documenting, and publicly disclosing Environmental Impact Statements (EIS), Environmental Assessments (EA), Categorical Exclusions (CE), and related NEPA decision documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption standard for EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt another agency's EIS when the adopting agency's proposed action is substantially the same as the action covered by the original EIS, subject to supplementation or reevaluation as necessary consistent with §1502.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is new or updated data, agencies can conduct additional analysis to determine whether supplementation criteria of §1502.9(d) are met or document why supplementation is not required. If the adopting agency determines the EIS requires supplemental analysis because the action is not substantially the same, the agency must treat the EIS as a draft, prepare the additional analysis, and publish the new draft EIS for notice and comment. Where a proposed action is not substantially the same, an agency must, at minimum, supplement the adopted EIS to ensure it adequately covers its proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption standard for EA
rubrics_metrics.description: An adopting agency may adopt another agency's environmental assessment (EA) and may supplement or reevaluate it as necessary in issuing its FONSI, but references to EAs in this section mean final EAs (not drafts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised the text to replace 'an environmental assessment' with 'another agency's environmental assessment' for clarity. CEQ interprets the regulatory text as precluding adoption of a draft EA; references to EA without specification mean a final EA. If an EA may require supplementation consistent with §1501.5(h), the adopting agency may adopt and supplement or reevaluate the EA as necessary and issue its FONSI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to supplementation/re-evaluation provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption provisions must be read consistent with the separate statutory/regulatory standards governing supplementation and reevaluation (e.g., §1502.9 and §1501.5(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ changed 'the statement requires supplementation' to 'the statement may require supplementation consistent with §1502.9 of this subchapter' to clarify agencies can analyze whether supplementation criteria are met or document why supplementation is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for adopting CE determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting another agency's categorical exclusion (CE) determination, the adopting agency must document a determination that the proposed action is substantially the same as the action covered by the original CE determination and that no extraordinary circumstances are present requiring preparation of an EA or EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ concluded agencies typically already make such determinations and that this documentation requirement will not be onerous. The documentation distinguishes adoption of another agency's CE determination from other reliance processes under §1501.4(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of CE adoptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must publicly disclose when they are adopting a CE determination (posting on an agency's website is acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed paragraphs (d)(1) and (d)(2) to require agencies to document and publish their adoptions of CE determinations; agencies have flexibility how to make information publicly available. CEQ declines to require multiple publication venues (website plus others) as unduly burdensome, but agencies may do so if they deem appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for environmental documents (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of who prepares an environmental document (agency, agency-directed contractor, or applicant under agency procedures), the agency must ensure the document is prepared with professional and scientific integrity using reliable data and resources, exercise independent judgment to review and take responsibility for the document, and briefly document its determination that the document meets NEPA, CEQ regulations, and the agency's NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects sections 102(2)(D) and (2)(E) of NEPA; CEQ revised the paragraph heading to 'agency responsibility' and added 'and direction' to clarify supervisory roles. CEQ declined to require agencies to more than briefly document this determination because the NEPA documents themselves generally demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'supervision' — supervision and direction
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ adds 'and direction' after 'supervision' to distinguish agency-directed contractors (agency supervises and directs contractor work) from applicant-directed contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction identifies contractors hired directly by the agency or third-party contractors paid by an applicant but supervised/directed by the agency, versus contractors hired and supervised by applicants (covered separately). CEQ declined to define 'supervision' in regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should outline applicant information needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should outline the information that the agency needs from the applicant to prepare an environmental document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retains prior regulatory language that helps ensure applicants know what information to provide for agency use in preparing NEPA documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency evaluation and responsibility for applicant-provided information
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must independently evaluate environmental information provided by an applicant and is responsible for the accuracy, scope, and contents of any applicant-provided environmental information included in the environmental document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ does not require agencies to specifically document their evaluation of each piece of applicant-provided information because agencies are responsible for preparing the NEPA document; requiring itemized documentation would be burdensome. Agencies have discretion to integrate applicant-provided information as they see fit but remain responsible for accuracy and legal compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may allow applicant-prepared EAs/EISs consistent with agency procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may allow applicants to prepare EAs or EISs consistent with agency procedures issued pursuant to section 107(f) of NEPA and §1507.3(c)(12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ notes the 2023 NEPA amendments require agencies to prescribe procedures to allow project sponsors to prepare EAs and EISs under agency supervision; CEQ uses and defines the term 'applicant' accordingly. Applicant-prepared documents remain subject to agency supervision, independent evaluation, and agency responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency guidance, participation, and supervision of agency-directed contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: For agency-directed contractors, agencies must provide their contractors guidance, and participate in and supervise the environmental document's preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (c)(1) requires active agency involvement in contractor work; paragraph (c)(2) requires independent agency evaluation and responsibility for contractor-prepared documents. CEQ did not limit this to particular document types because agencies may direct contractors to help draft any environmental document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent evaluation and documentation of contractor-prepared documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must independently evaluate contractor-prepared environmental documents, be responsible for their accuracy, scope, and contents, and document the evaluations in the environmental documents themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to prescribe detailed evaluation methods because levels of evaluation vary by context; however the regulations require documentation of the agency's evaluations in the NEPA documents (e.g., list of preparers, evaluation statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and qualifications of preparers and evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must include the names and qualifications of the persons preparing and independently evaluating contractor-prepared environmental documents (e.g., in the list of preparers for EISs), consistent with §1502.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires disclosure of who prepared and who independently evaluated the document to promote transparency and ability to assess professional/scientific integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor disclosure statements regarding financial interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency is responsible for preparing a disclosure statement for the contractor to execute, specifying that the contractor does not have any financial or other interest in the outcome of the proposed action (where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized §1506.5(c)(4) with 'where appropriate' modifying 'a cooperating agency' to address commenters' concerns. CEQ does not treat ordinary future engineering/design work by a firm as a per se conflict of interest, but encourages agencies to disclose potential future work in disclosure statements. A direct financial interest (e.g., contingency fee tied to agency authorization) would be a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and scientific integrity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must ensure the professional integrity, including scientific integrity, of the discussions and analyses in environmental documents (finalized as §1506.6(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is longstanding (since 1978) and consistent with NEPA section 102(2)(D). CEQ moves and preserves this core sentence as a standalone regulatory obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of high-quality information in preparing environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must use high-quality information in preparing environmental documents; CEQ provides examples such as 'reliable data and resources' and 'models'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ replaced language to require use of high-quality information 'in preparing environmental documents' (broader than only analyzing effects). CEQ references the Information Quality Act and other authorities regarding data quality and peer review as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Knowledge as an example of high-quality information
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous Knowledge is included as an example of high-quality information that agencies may rely on in NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ includes Indigenous Knowledge as an example but declines to define the term in the regulation; agencies may consult CEQ/OSTP guidance and Tribal consultation resources for implementation. Inclusion does not create a preference for Indigenous Knowledge over other scientific sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Best available science' not mandated as a regulation-wide requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ chose not to include 'best available science' as an explicit example in the final regulatory text to avoid implying an across-the-board requirement to use 'best available science' in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While CEQ considers 'best available science' one example of high-quality information, its regulatory omission avoids potential misinterpretation that NEPA requires a best-available-science standard in every instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of assumptions and model/method limitations (shall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall explain their assumptions and any limitations of their models and methods in environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adopted the proposed language but changed 'should' to 'shall' because disclosure of assumptions and limitations is necessary for the decision maker and public to assess the reliability of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of relying on existing information and undertaking new data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may rely on existing information as well as information obtained to inform the analysis; agencies may undertake new research or data collection when necessary to meet statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ replaced prior wording to make clear agencies should rely on existing information wherever possible but may also gather new or additional data (e.g., site surveys) as needed. CEQ removed the prior sentence saying agencies are not required to undertake new research, explaining that in some instances research is necessary to meet NEPA's analytic requirements. Agencies should exercise judgment and consider cost/time reasonableness.
